changes: p1 Rāmānuja: removed 'vidvas' from titles; viduṣā is only the epithet 'learned', not a title or office

p2 Samaravṛṣa: role changed from 'teacher' to 'other'. He is the commentator's teacher and played no part in making this copy. Confidence lowered to medium because the name may be a synonym form of Samarapuṅgava
Added p3 Deśika (Vedāntadeśika) as author of the root text Yatirājasaptati, from 'śrīdeśikakṛta-' in the colophon (medium confidence)
Notes: dropped the guess 'bade raver asti' (Sunday) and recorded the doubtful 'kā' and 'bader asti' instead

date.as_written: saṃvat 1799 miti kā caitrāṣṭamī bader asti

notes: The commentator Rāmānuja calls himself a pupil of Samaravṛṣadeśika. Since vṛṣa and puṅgava both mean 'bull', this is possibly a synonym form of Samarapuṅgava. The root text Yatirājasaptati is by Vedāntadeśika, named as 'śrīdeśika' in the colophon. No scribe, place or purpose is stated. Date: 'saṃvat 1799' can only be VS here (NS 1799 is impossible), giving about 1742 CE, which matches the catalogue. 'miti kā' is unclear: 'kā' might be a stray syllable or an abbreviation. 'bader asti' probably means 'badi' (dark fortnight) plus 'asti'. No weekday can be safely read from it, so the earlier reading 'raver' (Sunday) was dropped.
